required_changes: A rubric break can now be linked when the identical break outside the rubric would not be. The cause is that the rubric pass judges a rubric break in its own group, separate from the ordinary breaks of the same transclusion and edition (`_mark_choices(rubric, ordinary, position)`, scan_links.py:227). When no unit decides, `_choose` reaches the `earlier` step and the shared-prefix fallback, and there a group with one printing almost always chooses that printing. The rule in the docstring is that an earlier break 'chooses among the group's own', and here it doesn't. I traced this case by hand: an outer transclusion with no siddur: target holds `<tei:p><pb ed="1949 chol/minchah/a" n="e"/>x</tei:p>`, followed by `<p:transclude target="urn:prayer"><tei:note type="instruction"><pb ed="1949 chol/shacharit/b" n="r"/>rubric</tei:note><tei:p><pb ed="1949 chol/shacharit/b" n="s"/><pb ed="1949 chol/minchah/a" n="m"/>words</tei:p></p:transclude>`. The ordinary group is [shacharit/b, minchah/a], and the earlier hint {minchah/a} gives {minchah/a}: m is linked and s is not. The rubric group is [shacharit/b]. `_best` finds no match with {minchah/a}, and in the fallback `_shared('chol/shacharit/b', 'chol/minchah/a') == 1 > 0` gives {shacharit/b}, so r is linked. The result is a Shacharit page linked among the Minchah pages, which is the case `_choose`'s docstring warns about. If r were an ordinary break, it would not be linked. Fix: in the rubric pass, build `printings` from the ordinary and rubric breaks of the same (transclusion, edition) together, in document order. Keep `context` and `editions` ordinary-only, and set the result only on the rubric breaks. The ordinary choices stay unchanged. Add a scan_links test for the case above (r must not be linked).
limitations: I reviewed by reading only and ran no code or tests. Every behaviour described here, including the case in required_changes, comes from tracing the code by hand.

notes: Required change 1 from the last review (page-order inversion) is fixed. `_crosses_rubric_break` walks document order from the break to its target. It stops if it meets a marked break from the `rubric_ids` snapshot and keeps the moving break where it is. Breaks are attached last first, so a rubric break at the end of a rubric has already moved to the same target. The walk then meets it at its ('text') position before reaching its ('tail') target, so the snapshot keeps blocking after the move, as you said. The moved-barrier test does tell the two versions apart: without the barrier, pb1 would move next to pb2 and `_unmark_if_empty_page` would unmark it, giving ['2'] instead of ['1', '2'].

A rubric break in another column of the same parallel block is skipped by the role check, and the other-column test covers this. A rubric break outside every parallelItem still blocks a break inside a column. That's conservative and acceptable.

The walk in `_crosses_rubric_break` uses the same project filter as `_next_words`, so it should always reach the target. If it ever didn't, it would keep walking to the end of the document and could wrongly report a crossing. That's low risk, but a short comment noting the walk depends on `_next_words` taking the same path would help.

Presentation trade-off: a break kept back by the barrier stays where it was, often between blocks. In a parallel text that means a paragraph on its own with no partner in the other column, which is the case the move exists to prevent. Also, for `pb1 <note>pb2 words</note>` page 1 is empty, but both breaks stay linked: they aren't siblings, so `_unmark_if_empty_page` doesn't remove pb1. Before this change, two ordinary breaks there would have collapsed into one link. The last review allowed leaving the break in place, so I'm not requiring a change, but moving it to the start of the rubric (or unmarking it when no words come before the barrier) would be cleaner.

Required change 2 from the last review (selection isolation) is fixed for ordinary breaks. `_mark_choices(ordinary, ordinary, position)` gives exactly the old results: rubric breaks never enter `editions` or the `earlier` hint for ordinary text. The printing-isolation test checks the `earlier` path ([rubric, a, b] rather than [rubric, b]). The `editions` path isn't tested on its own, but the code guarantees it, because `editions` is built only from `context`, which is ordinary-only. The remaining problem runs the other way (the rubric break's own choice) and is the required change above.
A rubric break in an edition that has no ordinary breaks (`editions.get(edition, set())`) is linked through rule 4. The test covers it.
The module docstring now states all three rubric rules.
